newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall, employers seek deal in regional talks.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall, employers seek deal in regional talks.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall and employers will hold talks on Thursday aimed at reaching a regional deal on 1997 wages and sick pay which could serve as a pilot agreement for the whole of Germany.

Two weeks after negotiations at the national level broke down, negotiators in the southern German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg plan to talk about the 1997 wage round, sick pay as well as holiday and Christmas bonuses.
Both sides said they expected difficult negotiations. One day of talks has been scheduled.
The Baden-Wuerttemberg talks cover about 800,000 engineering workers including employees at Stuttgart-based Daimler-Benz AG.

IG Metall has staged several days of protests involving temporary stoppages by hundreds of thousands of workers. They demonstrated against planned cuts in pay to 80 percent during sickness, made possible by legislation which came into force last month.
Regional IG Metall chief Gerhard Zambelli and Dieter Hundt, the employers' chief negotiator, said they were aiming for a deal that could be adopted in other regions as well.
IG Metall wants to reinstate full pay during sickness while the employers' side has said any settlement must not increase the burden on employers.
